extracted.intended_audience: artists, writers, musicians, and readers interested in art theory and the moral/social purpose of art
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for producing and evaluating art that is accessible to the whole people, transmits feeling (especially religious/Christian perceptions of brotherhood), and favors clarity, simplicity, and social purpose over exclusivity and technical ostentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — art as transmission of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is the transmission of feeling the artist has experienced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: True art communicates an inner feeling from the artist into the feelings of others; evaluate art by how effectively it transmits that felt experience rather than by ornamental or technical display.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility / universality of art
rubrics_metrics.description: Artistic activity will be accessible to all men; the art of the future will be produced by and intelligible to the whole people, not merely upper classes or specialists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer works whose subject and form are open to everyone; avoid exclusivity that limits appreciation to a social elite.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form — clearness, simplicity, and brevity
rubrics_metrics.description: The demand will be for clearness, simplicity, and brevity in form rather than refined complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value brief, clear expression that transmits feeling without superfluities; consider short simple melodies, laconic stories, or sketches as superior forms when they authentically move people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter — feelings that unite (religious/Christian perception)
rubrics_metrics.description: The only subject-matter of the art of the future will be feelings drawing men towards union, or such as already unite them — especially the religious (Christian) perception of brotherhood.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select themes that evoke empathy, union, brotherhood, love of neighbour, and other feelings open to all; interpret common life from the Christian point of view to reveal fresh, moving emotions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique — redefined as clarity and compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Technique should be understood as the capacity briefly, simply, and clearly to transmit feeling; not as baroque complication or technical ostentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge 'technique' by clarity and expressive compression; de-emphasize virtuosity that masks absence of substance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern — rejection of 'art for art's sake' and exclusive aesthetics
rubrics_metrics.description: Art that exists for the sake of refinement, exclusivity, or to please only the cultured elite is a counterfeit of true art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid subject-matter and forms that appeal only to a narrow privileged circle (pride, spleen, satiety, voluptuousness); such art should be criticized as not fulfilling art's true purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of folk and children's forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Folk-art and children's art — jests, proverbs, riddles, songs, dances, lullabies, children's games, mimicry — are legitimate and important domains of art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider simple popular forms (fairy-tales, little songs, lullabies, riddles) as high-value artistic production when they genuinely touch many people and endure across generations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorial authenticity — artist must live common life
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound feeling can only be engendered when an artist is living on all sides the life natural and proper to mankind; the artist of the future will live the common life of man, earning subsistence by labour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works produced by those who experience ordinary life and struggle; be skeptical of art produced under conditions of luxury, security, or isolation from common experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Against professionalization and reliance on schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Art should not be produced only by professional artists paid for it; likewise professional schools are not the only or primary source of technique.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor broader education in elementary schools (singing and drawing for all) and learning from widespread examples of good art rather than exclusive professional training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and ethics — art should be widely diffused, not sold only for payment
rubrics_metrics.description: The artist of the future will wish to share the fruits of his spiritual strength with the greatest possible number and will be unable to understand an artist giving works only in exchange for payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess artistic practice by its willingness to reach broad audiences and to diffuse works widely rather than commodify them for a few.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form accessibility — forms open to everyone
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms of art will be such as will be open to everyone (simple songs, sketches, short narratives, unaccompanied melodies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer artistic forms that ordinary people can apprehend and reproduce; technical inaccessibility is a fault when it prevents transmission of feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter freshness through religious reinterpretation of common phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: Old, common phenomena (family relations, relations to country, animals, land) evoke fresh, unexpected, touching emotions when regarded from the Christian point of view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Look for new emotional insights in everyday subjects by reinterpreting them through a moral/religious lens rather than only seeking exotic historical or mythic topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure of excellence — universality over exclusivity; brevity over bulkiness
rubrics_metrics.description: The ideal of excellence will be universality of feeling and simplicity of form rather than exclusiveness and complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating works, prioritize their capacity to evoke common feeling across social strata and to do so succinctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value metric — lasting popular impact vs ephemeral elite diversion
rubrics_metrics.description: Composing a simple song or lullaby that touches millions is more important and fruitful than composing a novel or symphony that diverts some wealthy members briefly and is then forgotten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess value by breadth and longevity of emotional effect rather than by immediate prestige or technical ambition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art's social purpose — to train and evoke ethical feelings (brotherhood)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art is an organ of human life, transmitting reasonable perception into feeling, with the task to establish brotherly union among men and to train people to feel and act in accord with that perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate art by its capacity to inculcate social virtues (reverence for dignity, shame at luxury or violence, devotion to others) so that social cooperation is achieved by feeling rather than force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation to science — art depends on real science and religious perception
rubrics_metrics.description: Art always rests in intimate dependence on science; science decides the importance of feelings to be transmitted by art. True science should prioritize knowledge relevant to human life and religious perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer art grounded in a truthful social-scientific understanding of human life; critique art that reflects or is supported by a 'science for science's sake' that ignores social and moral truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-pattern — science for science's sake leads art astray
rubrics_metrics.description: Theories of 'art for art's sake' and 'science for science's sake' divert both fields from their true purpose and cause harmful selections of subject and method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be critical of art that serves merely aesthetic curiosity or fashionable technical novelty divorced from moral/social utility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training by example rather than formal schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Every true artist chiefly learns technique not in schools but in life, from examples of great masters; with many good artists producing, good examples will be more accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote diffusion of exemplary works and mentorship through communal exposure rather than narrow professional gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic condition effect on authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Security of maintenance (complete security and luxury) is injurious to an artist's productiveness because it removes him from the struggle necessary to engender sound feeling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When appraising art or the artist's practice, consider whether conditions of production have insulated the artist from ordinary human struggle and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opposition to art market intermediaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Until the dealers are driven out, the temple of art will not be a temple; the art of the future will drive them out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be skeptical of dealer-driven markets and gatekeepers that commodify art and restrict its diffusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Art as instrument for replacing enforced social order with voluntary cooperation
rubrics_metrics.description: Art should, through evoking feelings of brotherhood and union, cause external enforcement (law, police) to be set aside in favor of free joyous co-operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value works which have the demonstrable power to change customary behavior and social instincts toward mutual care and voluntary sacrifice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize moral and social knowledge over mere empirical curiosity
rubrics_metrics.description: Real science (and thereby art) should concentrate on religion, morality, and social life questions — how men should live — rather than on questions lacking direct relation to human life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art grounded in an understanding of social and moral truths will be judged higher than art motivated by purely technical or curious interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form-examples as standards of clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of desirable simple forms include a four-bar clear melody without accompaniment, a pencil-sketch that touches, a little song or fairy-tale that entertains or moves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these exemplars as practical standards when assessing whether a work achieves clear, simple, and memorable transmission of feeling.
